notes: Historical figures are taken from Equifax’s FY2025 10-K (operating revenue and operating income), with EBIT proxied by operating income as reported. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

D&A uses the consolidated cash flow statement line item “Depreciation and amortization.” Capex uses the consolidated cash flow statement line item “Capital expenditures.” ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

Net working capital (nwc) is computed (not directly stated) as: (Total current assets − cash and cash equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − short-term debt and current maturities of long-term debt). Sign flip in 2025 reflects short-term debt exceeding non-cash current assets under this construction.

Balance sheet components for NWC: FY2025 values from the FY2025 10-K balance sheet; FY2024/FY2023 values from the FY2024 annual report balance sheet. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

Assumed tax_rate (0.24) is a base-case average near Equifax’s reported effective rates across recent years; forward effective rate is not explicitly guided in the filing. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))
WACC and terminal assumptions (WACC=0.085, terminal_growth=0.02) are base-case modeling assumptions and are not directly disclosed by the company.

NOL balance is based on total net operating loss carryforwards disclosed in the FY2025 10-K (U.S. federal/state + foreign). ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

NOL utilization percent (0.80) is assumed using a standard NOL utilization framing because the filing excerpt provided NOL balances/expiration but not an explicit utilization-rate parameter for DCF use.
Investments is set to null because the DCF input package does not include a separate forward acquisitions/investments schedule; acquisitions/divestitures are not separately forecast here.

catalysts: Changes in U.S. and international credit/verification volumes (driven by consumer lending, hiring, and mortgage activity) that impact demand for Equifax’s products.
Technology transformation execution and amortization/reinvestment cycle affecting operating margin and free cash flow conversion.
Regulatory and compliance outcomes that could alter dispute-handling costs or long-term product demand dynamics.
Capital allocation updates (share repurchases/dividends) based on leverage and liquidity conditions.
company_overview: Equifax operates through three segments: Workforce Solutions, U.S. Information Solutions, and International. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

Workforce Solutions includes Verification Services and Employer Services. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

U.S. Information Solutions includes Online Information Solutions and Financial Marketing Services. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

International provides information services products across Latin America, Europe, Asia Pacific, and Canada. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 operating revenue was 6,074,500,000 with operating income of 1,095,200,000 (operating margin 0.180). ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

FY2025 cash provided by operating activities was 1,615,700,000 and capital expenditures were 481,400,000. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

Reported FY2025 effective tax rate in the filing ranged from ~0.232 to ~0.251 across jurisdictions/years, supporting a base-case tax-rate assumption near 0.24. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

FY2025 diluted weighted-average shares were 124.1 million, anchoring per-share conversion for the equity value bridge. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth decelerates from 2025 into 2030 to reflect a maturing credit/verification demand profile (mid-single-digit by 2028-2030).

EBIT margin is modeled to stabilize and slightly improve toward ~0.183 by 2030, consistent with recent operating margin levels and modest expense leverage. ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))

Capital intensity normalizes versus the 2023 spike (capex as % sales declines vs. 2023-2024 history and stabilizes in the high-0.08s). ([investor.equifax.com](https://investor.equifax.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000033185-26-000010/efx-20251231.htm))
Working capital is modeled to revert from 2025’s temporarily negative net working capital into a small positive requirement over the forecast horizon (see NWC definition in notes).
key_risks: Credit cycle downside: lower inquiries/transactions could reduce revenue growth and pressure margin.
Regulatory, data-quality, or cybersecurity events could drive incremental costs and/or reputational damage.
FX volatility materially impacts reported International results and may affect margins and growth rate assumptions.
Market discount-rate repricing (higher WACC) or weaker terminal economics could reduce equity value.
